answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake and continuously solve small verifiable tasks - a cipher puzzle bound to its public key - before earning trust. Like a vine that only climbs where it can grip, reputation grows only through sustained, costly work: a new account starts with a walnut-sized stake and near-zero weight, so spinning up thousands of fake identities means locking thousands of stakes and paying compute for each, while honest agents amortize one stake over a long useful life.
